event: Industrial Canal floodwall breaches flood the Lower Ninth Ward and on into Arabi, St. Bernard Parish, during Hurricane Katrina

minuteZero.what: Mayor Nagin announces the first-ever mandatory evacuation of New Orleans.
minuteZero.why: It is the order that covers every Lower Ninth Ward household, so it is when a coordinator would start calling. Both federal reports put it at about 11 a.m.; secondary accounts say 9:30-10 a.m.

events.what: Mandatory evacuation of New Orleans ordered.
IHNC at the lock about 5.7 ft NAVD88(2004.65), rising about 1 ft an hour.

Earliest water into the north of the ward (eyewitnesses at Site 3 and OP-5). IPET: one or both IHNC breaches failed before 05:30, possibly as early as 04:30. ILIT and Team Louisiana put both breaches at 07:30-07:45; the court (Duval 2011) puts the north breach at about 06:00.
Stopped clocks at Site C1, next to the north breach, read 05:15 at +2 ft NAVD88; ground there is about -6 ft, so the water had risen about 8 ft.
Pump station OP-5 shut down for high water.
Katrina makes landfall near Buras, LA, at 110 kt (1110 UTC).
Higher clocks at Site C1 stop at 06:30 (about +4 ft NAVD88).
New Orleans Lakefront (KNEW): 60 kt sustained, 75 kt gust (incomplete record).

South breach (about 850 ft, starting about 300 ft north of N. Claiborne Ave) opens; barge ING 4727 is carried through it. Team Louisiana: 'consensus' 07:30; ILIT 07:45; IPET: walls overtopped about 07:30.
events.where: p. 67; ILIT Ch. 6 p. 6-6; IPET V App. 14 p. V-14-23

events.what: Jackson Barracks (ground about +4 ft) still dry in a time-stamped photo.
Water reaches Jackson Barracks from the north; up to truck wheels by 08:13.

In Chalmette, east of Paris Road and outside the map, water from the marsh to the north-east arrives as 'waves of black water' (Channel 8 tower camera, Magistrate St and Marietta Dr); houses in Corinne Estates are 8-10 ft deep by 09:00-09:30 and the water peaks there at about 10.8 ft.

The 40 Arpent back levee (crown 7-9 ft) is overtopped massively from the filled St. Bernard wetland, flooding St. Bernard east of Paris Road. The IHNC breaches and Caernarvon overtopping account for about 10 percent of the St. Bernard basin's flooding.
IHNC peaks at about 14.3 ft NAVD88(2004.65) at the lock.
Final landfall near the Louisiana/Mississippi border (1445 UTC).
The ward's water moving east meets Chalmette's near Paris Road 'in the midmorning timeframe' (10:00 is our reading of 'midmorning').
Water in the ward peaks at about 10.5 ft NAVD88(2004.65) at Jackson Barracks (IPET text gives 1945 UTC, 14:45; the plotted point is about 13:42). IPET: 10.5-11 ft for the Lower Ninth and St. Bernard.
St. Bernard Parish unwatering complete on approximately 15 September (no separate date published for the Lower Ninth).
Hurricane Rita reopens the large south breach and refloods the Upper and Lower Ninth Ward.
USACE reports all floodwater removed from New Orleans.

outcome.deaths: 73 victims recovered in the Lower Ninth Ward (Team Louisiana App. III Table A3.2; Boyd 2011 gives 72); 71 within one mile of the two IHNC breaches (Table A3.3)
